text:
amelia: Heads up — we just saw a big throughput drop in us-west-2 around 11:12 UTC. p95 spiked from 220ms -> 1.1s and request success rate for the gen route fell ~12%. Appears correlated with GPU OOMs and worker restarts on the inference pool. :rotating_light:

ops-bot: ALERT: high_oom_rate on rw-infer-pool-usw2 (alert link: https://ops.redwood.example/alerts/8932)

sanjay: which model variant / commit? did anything change in kernel selection or batching configs recently?

amelia: Rollout affected pool uses commit 1a2b3c4 — there was a kernel-selection heuristic change deployed 36h ago (prefer fused attention for seq<=512). Also we pushed a small batching tweak that increases max_batch_window to 12ms.

maria: Hmm. The OOMs look like fragmentation rather than total allocs. Snippet from node logs: ```
[2026-03-18T11:12:07Z] cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (requested 2147483648)
[2026-03-18T11:12:07Z] worker-17: restarting (oom)
[2026-03-18T11:12:09Z] allocator: free 512MB, largest_free 190MB, total_free 1.2GB
```

tarun: That largest_free size is the giveaway — fragmentation. Are we seeing long-lived KV caches pinned per-request? Any pattern in prefix lengths?

amelia: Yes — traffic skew to long-chat prefixes from a customer test. KV cache for those sessions grows to ~1.6GB per worker. We have eviction but it's by LRU per session, and restarts cause cold misses so downstream latency is higher.

lena: Also noticed kernel selection fallback: when sequence len fluctuates, we hit fused kernels then fallback to split kernels and fragmentation increases since the allocation patterns differ. Profile dump attached: ```
Profiler summary (worker-17):
- fused_attention kernel hotpath allocations: 3 blocks (~256MB each)
- split_attention path: many small allocations (~4-16MB) leading to fragmentation
- peak_gpu_mem: 13.2GB (12GB card)
```

sanjay: So combined: bigger batches (12ms window) + fused kernel allocations + long-lived KV = fragmentation -> occasional large alloc fails -> worker restart -> throughput drop. Makes sense.

maria: Quick mitigation options? Suggest: 1) revert batching window to 6ms, 2) pin kernel selection to conservative split kernels for this pool, 3) force rolling recycle of workers to reclaim fragmented memory.

tarun: I'm ready to roll revert for batching window. Can someone push a canary with kernel-selection pinned to split kernels for 10% of traffic? We should validate latency regressions.

amelia: Starting canary now -> routing 10% to pool-3 with kernel_policy=split. Will monitor.

ops-bot: DEPLOY: canary started by amelia (deploy 1764123620).

lena: After canary: p95 on canary nodes back to 230ms, no OOMs observed in 8m. Main pool still seeing sporadic OOMs.

sanjay: Good signal. Maria, can you coordinate rolling restart of the remaining nodes once we revert batching? We want to avoid full-cluster restart at once.

maria: On it. I'll schedule draining 2 nodes at a time, restart, verify KV residency and fragmentation numbers.

amelia: Also adding a temporary allocator compaction flag (runtime flag: GPU_ALLOC_COMPACT=1) to test if compaction reduces largest_free fragmentation. I'll enable on canary first.

tarun: If compaction works, we can bake into next runtime release. But need to validate perf hit. Compaction might add latency on allocs.

lena: Observed compaction experiment: small increase in median allocation latency (~1.5ms) but p95 improved because OOMs gone. Tradeoff seems acceptable for now.

maria: Rolling revert of batching window to 6ms completed on remaining nodes. No new OOMs in 20m. Throughput back to expected baseline.

sanjay: Follow-ups: 1) Revert kernel-selection heuristic until we have a more fragmentation-aware selector. 2) Add better eviction for KV cache based on global memory pressure (not just per-session LRU). 3) Add per-worker allocator fragmentation metrics to SLI. 4) Perf test compaction impact at scale.

amelia: Filing a GH issue with reproduction notes + logs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/1246 (includes steps to reproduce with long-prefix load, sample profile, nvidia-smi logs).

ops-bot: INCIDENT-8932 updated: mitigated (canary + revert).

tarun: Thanks everyone. I'll own the kernel selector fix (make it fragmentation-aware + prefer consistent allocation patterns across requests).

lena: I'll own the KV eviction change and add a canary flag to evict under global mem pressure.

maria: I'll add the rolling restart playbook to the incidents repo and include a checklist for fragmentation-induced OOMs.

amelia: Closing notes: immediate mitigation = revert batching window + pin kernels + rolling restarts. Longer-term = allocator improvements, smarter kernel selection, KV eviction by global pressure.

sanjay: Great postmortem material. Add perf numbers + before/after profiler screenshots to the incident page and we'll review in eng-all-hands. :thumbsup:
